scenes.text: You take a photo a few streets from home. You switch location off, and post it. Private, right?

Not quite. A stranger can give your photo to an AI that reads what's in it: a street sign, a shop name, a building. Clues like these give you away. Strangers' Eyes shows you what that AI sees, before you post.

One: your device covers faces and private words with solid blocks, and strips hidden photo data. Two: Google's Gemini, in the cloud, plays the stranger, and sees only that cleaned copy. Three: your private list, home, work, child's name, never leaves your device. It checks how close the guess came, and never tells the cloud if it was right. Four: fix it, and attack again.
Now the real app, in Judge Mode: free-to-use photos of public places, and a made-up family with a child called Lucas.
This castle photo has a lunchbox labelled Lucas. Your device finds the name and covers it, before the photo is sent.
We took the cover off on purpose. A last checkpoint inspects every request to the AI. It found the name and stopped it. That copy never reached the attacker.

Cover back on, the copy goes out. These are real Gemini answers, recorded on November twenty-third and replayed. The AI recognised the castle. The app never shows where the AI thinks you are, only how close it came: within one kilometre of home, and of work. You can't cover a castle, so the app says: crop it, or don't post it.

This one can be fixed. The AI read a street sign and its house-number plate, and found the street, within five kilometres of home and work. The app covers both, then attacks again. Now it can only guess the city. Risk reduced, with the AI's confidence shown. Never a guarantee.
But covering isn't always enough. With the sign hidden, the AI still found the right city from the building itself. Still exposed.

In our test of ten public-place photos, the AI placed five within five kilometres, and never refused to guess. Covering the clues it named moved its guess further from the real spot for three of four re-tested photos.

That's hybrid AI: the cloud brings world knowledge, your device keeps the secrets. Private steps run on Gemini Nano in Chrome, or on Apple's own model on iPhone, shown here in the iOS app. No on-device AI? Simple rules take over, never the cloud. Built on Firebase AI Logic.
Location off isn't location hidden. See what a stranger's AI sees, before you post. Strangers' Eyes.
